# The cache contract (three tiers)

Every data route falls into exactly one tier. Extracted verbatim from CLAUDE.md; know which tier a route is in before touching it.

- **The cache contract (three tiers)** — every data route falls into exactly one of these; know which tier a route is in before touching it:
  1. **GraphQL org-repos — byte-identical, identity-test-locked (unchanged).** `POST /graphql`'s org-repos query is assembled in `graphql.go` to match exactly GitHub's selection set, locked by an identity test (`identity_shape_test.go`). This is the ONLY route where byte-identity to GitHub applies. The assembly reads global truth **filtered by the reveal layer** (`ListVisibleReposByOwner`: public repos + the principal's granted repos), so the served view tracks what GitHub itself answers this principal — never the whole truth store. The assembly additionally **skips `is_archived` rows**: the locked selection says `repositories(isArchived: false)`, so GitHub itself never returns an archived repo here and the node carries no `isArchived` field for a client to filter on — but truth DOES hold archived repos (the fleet refresher's owner query has no such filter), so before this the mirror answered with rows GitHub would have withheld and no consumer could tell. Filtered in `graphql.go`, not in `ListVisibleReposByOwner`: the reason is this route's contract, not a property of what the reveal layer permits. The backing fetch (`OrgReposFetcher`) runs with the PRINCIPAL'S OWN token, merges the snapshot into global truth (`SyncOrgTruth`: upsert + reconcile, never delete-then-insert), and replace-syncs the principal's grants. Known bounded caveat: the locked selection pages labels at `first: 10`, so a lazy sync stores a 10-label snapshot per PR (a >10-label PR is truncated on this path — the contract forbids extending the query; the App-driven owner query reads 100 and the apply mode corrects the stored set). Any other GraphQL query forwards to the passthrough (a `mutation` is recorded as a `write`).
  2. **Cached REST routes — global state absorbed, rebuilt TRIMMED, revealed by permission.** `internal/api/respcache*.go` (one file per route family — `_contents`, `_gitcommits`, `_commits`, `_commitci`, `_compare`, `_pulls`, `_pulldiff`, `_pullfiles`, `_branches`, `_repo`, `_installation`, `_installationrepos`, `_actionsruns`, `_labels`, `_hooks`, `_ratelimit` — with `respcache.go` itself holding only the machinery they share) + `internal/ghdata/respcache*.go`. Every read of GLOBAL state passes the reveal gate first (`reveal(r, owner, repo, kind, key)`): public repo / live grant / cached deny verdict / live probe — a denied caller gets GitHub's own relayed answer, an unrevealable transient error 502s that one request, and a successful probe absorbs the probed repo object into truth and records a grant. The exceptions are the routes whose answer is not global state at all but one credential's own (the `access_tokens` mint, the installation lookups, `installation/repositories`), plus the ADMIN-only hook listings, where the reveal layer is not merely unnecessary but INSUFFICIENT — it proves READ access and its public fast path admits any principal, so a global row would leak a repo's webhook endpoints to a read-only caller. All of them key the row by the app identity or the bearer's fingerprint, which is self-gating: a stored answer can only ever be replayed to the credential GitHub already answered it for. The route ABSORBS the state a GitHub response contains into structured columns and REBUILDS the response from that state, **dropping every URL field**: `url`, anything matching `*_url`, and `_links` (locked by `assertNoURLKeys` in `respcache_fixture_test.go`) — EXCEPT a per-route **pinned allowlist** of consumer-read link fields (the helper takes exact key names; today: the statuses `target_url`, the check-run `details_url`/`html_url`, and the workflow-run `html_url`, all rendered by the required-builds hook — consumer survey 2026-07-11 — plus the hook listings' `config.url`). Adding an allowlist entry requires a fresh consumer survey, with ONE other ground: `config.url` is not a link into GitHub's API at all but the hook's own destination, the field that says which hook this is, so a listing without it answers nothing and no survey could change that. Every other URL key stays banned. Hits AND misses both serve the rebuilt shape, marked `X-GSM-Cache: hit|miss`; rebuilt responses carry only `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Anything a route cannot model passes through verbatim, unstored, recorded as `passthrough`: non-default `Accept` media types, unknown query params, symlink/submodule objects, >1 MiB `"encoding":"none"` files, oversized bodies, unexpected statuses. The v1 routes:
     The route families, each with its absorb/rebuild/guard/invalidation detail in **docs/cache/rest-routes.md**: repo `contents` (+ the 404 absent answer) · immutable `git/commits/{sha}` (+ expiring 404 miss markers) · the `commits` LIST · `compare/{basehead}` (+ 404 unknown-ref verdicts) · the commit-CI trio (`commits/{ref}/status`, `/check-runs`, the statuses list under both spellings) · the `access_tokens` mint · the open-PR list · the single PR (+ closed-PR docs, merge-field staleness, diff 406 verdicts) · repo and owner `installation` lookups (+ the 404 "not installed here" verdict) · `installation/repositories` · the repo and org webhook-config listings (`hooks`) · PR `files` · PR `commits` · `branches` · the single `labels/{name}` read · `actions/runs` (two shapes: the per-commit `?head_sha=` SNAPSHOT, and the repo-wide `?status=`/`?branch=` listing REBUILT from webhook-maintained `workflow_runs` truth behind a completeness marker — never a snapshot, because clearing one per job delivery is invalidate-and-refetch) · the Actions job reads (`actions/runs/{id}/jobs`, `actions/jobs/{id}`) · `git/ref/{ref}` · Code Quality `setup` (config with no webhook: flushed by the PATCH the mirror proxies, short TTL) · the bare repo read.
     `GET /rate_limit` is in this tier but has no store row and no miss: it is answered entirely from `internal/ratemeter`'s passively observed `X-RateLimit-*` headers, so the route NEVER calls upstream — a credential the meter has not observed gets an honestly empty `resources` object rather than a fetch. Why a TTL-bounded row would be wrong for it, and what the mirror still cannot see: **docs/cache/uncacheable-routes.md**.
     There is **no "correctly uncached" verdict** (operator ruling 2026-08-06: "never encourage bypassing the cache for any reason. Bypassing the cache is a hack that means we need something fixed in github-state-mirror"). A route that still forwards is unfinished work; a resource no delivery names today is a missing invalidation signal to go add. The same doc's "Still forwarding" section records what each remaining route still needs, so a pass starts from the open question — never as permission to leave it.
     Truth rows are global; the reveal layer is what keeps callers apart. Invalidation deletes are global too (a webhook is a global fact). Every response-cache table is pruned on write: expired rows plus LRU beyond `ghdata.CacheMaxRows` (default 1,000,000; set at startup from the `CACHE_MAX_ROWS` env var — unparseable/<1 fails startup — and lowered directly by tests). One knob for every table on purpose: all but `git_commits_cache` are TTL-bounded, so the cap is only a runaway safety net for them; `git_commits_cache` (immutable rows, no TTL) is the one table that actually grows to the ceiling. Dispositions land in the request log: `hit` (served from state), `miss` (fetched+absorbed, with upstream status), `passthrough` (read forwarded/replayed unstored), `write` (mutation proxied), `error`.
  3. **Everything else — verbatim passthrough, uncached.** Transparently reverse-proxied to GitHub via `newGitHubProxy` (`internal/api/proxy.go`), wired as chi's `NotFound`/`MethodNotAllowed` (so the `Use` middleware — CORS, recoverer — still wraps it); the GraphQL handler forwards any non-org query the same way. The proxy forwards the caller's `Authorization` verbatim (never the server token), rejects tokenless requests with 401, targets `gh.BaseURL()` (tests hit the fake upstream), and `ModifyResponse` strips GitHub's duplicate `Access-Control-Allow-*` while keeping `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`. A 2xx passthrough under `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` refreshes the caller's grant (GitHub just proved access — `refreshGrantOn2xx`). Mutating methods are logged as `write`, not `passthrough` — a write is proxied because it mutates, not because caching failed. Do NOT make this path touch the freshness store.

     **Passthrough DEBOUNCING** (`internal/api/debounce.go`, operator directive 2026-07-26) sits between the recorder and the proxy: an eligible uncacheable READ is HELD for `PASSTHROUGH_DEBOUNCE` (default 5s) instead of being forwarded immediately; every identical request arriving during the window joins the same batch, and when the window closes ONE upstream call is made and its response replayed to every member. Both effects are intended — fleet-sweep polling of unmodelable endpoints collapses to one call per window, AND uncacheable endpoints become visibly slow, pricing an unmodelable read into the caller's own latency (`X-GSM-Debounce: <ms>` + `X-GSM-Debounce-Batch: <n>` make the charge legible). **The security property that must never regress: a batch is keyed by the caller's CREDENTIAL** (SHA-256 fingerprint of the bearer token) — the passthrough has no reveal gate, so sharing one caller's answer with another's request would hand out data GitHub never agreed to show them; the key also covers the request URI verbatim, `Accept`, and `X-GitHub-Api-Version` (`TestDebounce_NeverSharesAcrossCredentials` pins it). Eligibility is GET only (a mutation is an intent, not a shared answer), bearer token present, no request body, and **no conditional/`Range` headers** — a 304 against one caller's etag is a wrong answer for anyone else; every ineligible request forwards immediately, undelayed. The batch's fetch runs on a `context.WithoutCancel`-derived context (the freshness-fetch doctrine) so one waiter hanging up can't kill the others' answer, and once its call is issued the batch is CLOSED (a later arrival opens a fresh one — a response is never served to a request that arrived after the call answering it). Bounded by 1024 concurrent batches and an 8 MiB buffered body; past either, requests forward directly/refetch individually (correct, just uncoalesced). HEAD is excluded from eligibility too: it is rare here and its bodyless response would need its own replay path. The debounce key's components are length-delimited before hashing, so no concatenation of one field can imitate another, and the digest keeps the map key bounded whatever the caller sends. `Debouncer.Drain` cuts every pending window short (waiters are still on the wire — answer them now) and waits out in-flight fetches; `cmd/server` drains it BEFORE the freshness manager. Observability: each waiter is still its own recorded `passthrough` with its own reason and its real end-to-end duration (the hold included), the batch's single mirror→GitHub leg is charted once as an `upstream` event (so the Timeline shows N long inbound bars containing ONE real call), and the route group carries `debounced`/`upstream_saved` — two counters on purpose, since held-with-nothing-saved means the polls arrive further apart than the window: all cost, no benefit.

- **Uncached-traffic SHAPE capture + the implementation brief** — `internal/api/shapes.go` samples what the request-group counters cannot hold: per route shape, the UNION of query-parameter NAMES, the Accepts, the callers, the upstream statuses, and the key/type SKELETON of GitHub's response. **No value is ever retained** — scalars become type names, arrays collapse to their element shape, objects keep only key names, and a non-JSON body yields no skeleton at all (which is the answer: an opaque body has no state to absorb, so it cannot be a tier-2 route). Bounded and cheap: at most one body sample per route shape per 30 min, 256 KiB cap (abandoned past it, never truncated), 300 shapes, in-memory on the requestLog stance. Sampling hooks the two paths that forward reads — `recordPassthrough` (every proxied request) and `replayUnstored` (request modeled, response not — the class whose answer the brief most needs). `GET /api/brief` (admin) joins it to the route groups, ranks by passthrough volume, and renders Markdown carrying the tier-2 checklist and the files a new route touches, so the output is actionable rather than a pile of numbers. See **docs/dashboard/implementation-brief.md**.
  Adding a cached REST route means tier 2: reveal gate + global structured state + trimmed rebuild + the recursive no-URL-keys invariant test + explicit invalidation/TTL/pruning — never verbatim byte replay, and never a byte-identity requirement (that is tier 1's, only).
